skills.name: alignment
skills.title: Alignment
skills.description: Measures a running page for edges, gaps, centring and radii that miss by a pixel or two, then judges visual weight and returns a numbered report with proof.
skills.summary: Measure spacing, edges, centering, and visual weight in a running page.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: animate
skills.title: Animate
skills.description: Build an animation from scratch, making the decisions in the order that determines whether it feels right — should it animate at all, what purpose, which tool, which properties, which curve and duration, how it interrupts, how it exits. Writes the implementation. Use when asked to animate something, add motion, make a component feel alive, or build a transition. For critiquing existing motion use review-animations; for auditing a whole codebase use improve-animations.
skills.summary: Build purposeful web animations, from the first decision to the final frame.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: animate-expo
skills.title: Animate for Expo
skills.description: Build animations in React Native and Expo, making the decisions in the order that determines whether they feel right — should it animate, which thread it runs on, which properties, spring or timing, how the gesture hands off, how it degrades. Writes the implementation with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router and expo-haptics. Use when animating anything in an Expo app, adding gestures, sheets, screen transitions, press feedback or haptics, or fixing motion that stutters on device. For web animation use `animate`.
skills.summary: Author native motion and gestures with Expo and Reanimated.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: animation-performance
skills.title: Animation performance
skills.description: Keep web animations inside the frame budget — animate composite-only properties, keep motion off the main thread when the page is busy, and find the cause when an animation drops frames. Covers the layout/paint/composite pipeline, cheaper property swaps, CSS vs WAAPI vs requestAnimationFrame, Motion's hardware-accelerated path, React re-rendering per frame, inherited CSS variable recalculation, blur cost, and when `will-change` actually helps. Use when an animation is janky, choppy, stutters, or drops frames; when choosing which property to animate; when deciding between CSS and JS animation on performance grounds; or when reaching for `will-change` or GPU layers. For choosing easing, duration, or whether to animate at all use animate; for reviewing motion as a whole use review-animations.
skills.summary: Find dropped frames and keep motion within the rendering budget.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: animation-vocabulary
skills.title: Animation vocabulary
skills.description: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.
skills.summary: Find the right name for the motion you have in mind.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: apple-design
skills.title: Apple design
skills.description: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.
skills.summary: Apply physical gestures, springs, materials, and typography to interfaces.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: ask-sonner
skills.title: Sonner toasts
skills.description: Guide to Sonner, the React toast library — install and wire up the Toaster, pick the right toast() call, promise and loading toasts, updating, dismissing and persisting toasts, styling, theming and icons, positioning and multiple toasters. Use when working with Sonner or troubleshooting it — toasts that don't appear, appear twice, lose their styles, ignore Tailwind classes, sit behind a modal, or don't follow dark mode.
skills.summary: Build and troubleshoot React toast notifications with Sonner.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: audit
skills.title: Audit
skills.description: Reviews a change, a session or a whole codebase against every skill in this collection and returns one ranked, numbered report.
skills.summary: Get a ranked review across the full interface skills collection.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: avatar
skills.title: Avatar
skills.description: Draws any object as a flat character with two capsule eyes, then animates its whole body so it glances, blinks, breathes, follows the pointer and falls asleep.
skills.summary: Turn an object into an expressive, animated character.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: blank-page
skills.title: Blank page
skills.description: Turn a one-line motion / animation / design brief into the full prompt: a committed look grounded in five reference images, three motion references, numbered beats with a turn, and the refs and assets attached. Also tightens edit notes. Use for "/blank-page", "expand this prompt", "make this prompt more specific", "what is missing from this prompt", "help me write the prompt for X", or whenever a one-line animation / composition / design brief is about to be handed to an agent.
skills.summary: Turn a one-line creative brief into a grounded motion direction.
skills.author: Stewdio

skills.name: bots
skills.title: Bots
skills.description: Turns chosen Grok Bots into a shakeable pile, portfolio cards and an org chart page, each with a link to copy the bot, with private details stripped.
skills.summary: Build a portfolio for the Grok Bots you choose to share.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: break-ui
skills.title: Break UI
skills.description: Try to break a piece of UI by feeding it worst-case data — long names, unbreakable emails, one-letter names, missing fields, huge counts, zero items, long labels, non-Latin text, emoji, extreme numbers — then render it behind a "Demo data / Worst case" toggle and report everything that broke, with the fix for each. Use when the user asks to stress-test, break, or find edge cases in a component or screen, or to "try the worst case". For visual design critique use emil-design-eng; for motion use review-animations.
skills.summary: Stress-test a screen with realistic worst-case data.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: color
skills.title: Color
skills.description: Holds text and control contrast to exact ratios, routes colour through role tokens and gives dark mode its own palette.
skills.summary: Check contrast, semantic color roles, and dark-mode palettes.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: copy
skills.title: Copy
skills.description: Writes interface labels in Title Case, short and plain, with one-line descriptions and no em dashes.
skills.summary: Write short, clear labels and interface descriptions.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: deconstruct
skills.title: Deconstruct
skills.description: Breaks an animation or interaction into a state machine and a timeline of every property, on a page you can scrub and edit.
skills.summary: Break an interaction into states and a timeline you can inspect.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: defaults
skills.title: Defaults
skills.description: Applies house defaults for scroll edges, surfaces, type, sound, focus, forms, loading, hotkeys and dialogs.
skills.summary: Establish the details that make a screen feel finished.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: emil-design-eng
skills.title: Design engineering
skills.description: This skill encodes Emil Kowalski's philosophy on UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great.
skills.summary: Review UI craft, polish, component details, and motion decisions.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: find-animation-opportunities
skills.title: Find animation opportunities
skills.description: Search a codebase or UI for places that don't animate but should, and reject everything that shouldn't. Read-only; it proposes motion with exact values, it does not implement it. Use when the user asks "what could be animated here?" or wants to "make this feel more alive". For fixing existing animations, use improve-animations or review-animations instead.
skills.summary: Find the few moments where motion would actually help.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: frames
skills.title: Frames
skills.description: Records a performance trace of one interaction on a throttled CPU, names what drops frames or delays input, then proves the fix with a second trace.
skills.summary: Measure interaction performance and prove the improvement.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: gather
skills.title: Gather
skills.description: Collects references from the user's own library, their boards and pattern sites onto one linked board before a design is built.
skills.summary: Collect visual references before starting a design.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: icons
skills.title: Icons
skills.description: Draws missing icons in the project's own style, measured from every icon the set already has and built to morph, then shows the set on one sheet.
skills.summary: Fill gaps in an icon set while keeping its existing style.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: improve-animations
skills.title: Improve animations
skills.description: Survey a codebase's animation and motion code as a senior motion advisor, then produce a prioritized audit and self-contained implementation plans for other agents (or cheaper models) to execute. Read-only on source code — it plans improvements, it does not apply them. Use when the user asks to "improve the animations", "audit the motion", "make this app feel better", or wants a roadmap of animation fixes rather than a review of a single diff.
skills.summary: Audit motion and write practical implementation plans.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: keyboard
skills.title: Keyboard
skills.description: Walks a running page with the keyboard alone, records every focus stop and reports controls it cannot reach, see or operate.
skills.summary: Check an interface using only the keyboard.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: lab
skills.title: Lab
skills.description: Builds a temporary page that shows every variant and state of real components at once, each linked to its source.
skills.summary: Show real components, variants, and states in one temporary workspace.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: match
skills.title: Match
skills.description: Rebuilds a named reference from its real source and computed values, then compares the two side by side.
skills.summary: Recreate a reference from measured values and compare the result.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: mobile-native
skills.title: Mobile native
skills.description: Make a web app feel native on a phone — the small CSS and meta-tag fixes that separate "a website in a browser" from something that feels installed. Covers sticky hover states, tap highlight flashes, the 100vh bug, inputs that zoom the page, laggy taps, pull-to-refresh hijacking scroll, content under the notch, long-press selecting button text, carousels that scroll the wrong way, mismatched status bars, and the rule that you test on real hardware. Use when a web app is being built for or reviewed on mobile, when something "works in Chrome but feels wrong on my phone", when building a PWA, a bottom sheet, a carousel, a full-screen layout, or any touch interaction. For motion itself use animate; for React Native use animate-expo.
skills.summary: Polish mobile web behavior, touch targets, scrolling, and safe areas.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: motion
skills.title: Motion
skills.description: Applies house motion for what animates, easing, durations, springs, gestures, exits, motion blur and reduced motion.
skills.summary: Set consistent durations, easing, gestures, and reduced-motion behavior.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: pick-ui-library
skills.title: Pick a UI library
skills.description: Pick the right library for a given frontend task from a curated, opinionated list — numbers, OTP inputs, charts, command menus, virtualization, drag and drop, toasts, state, styling, and more. Only runs when explicitly invoked; it does not trigger on its own.
skills.summary: Choose a maintained library for a specific interface problem.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: playful-design-router
skills.title: Playful Design Router
skills.description: Routes interface and design work to the right installed design skill (Emil Kowalski's design-engineering and animation skills, Benji Taylor's stageshow, Vercel's web-design-guidelines, Stewdio's blank-page and Raphael Salaja's userinterface collection). Use at the start of any UI, visual design, motion, copy, layout, mockup or front-end polish task, when reviewing or shipping interface changes, or whenever it is unclear which design skill applies.
skills.summary: Choose the right design skill for the task at hand.
skills.author: Playful Design

skills.name: prose
skills.title: Prose
skills.description: Writes posts and breakdowns that open on where the author stands, show the options that lost, give exact numbers and mark every guess as a guess.
skills.summary: Write clear posts, case studies, and design breakdowns.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: prototype
skills.title: Prototype
skills.description: Builds several real, labelled variants of one idea on a single page so the user can pick, then deletes the rest.
skills.summary: Compare several working design directions before choosing one.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: remove-animations
skills.title: Remove animations
skills.description: Find the animations an interface doesn't need and remove them — motion on keyboard actions, high-frequency surfaces, functional data, and decoration with no purpose — then clean up what they leave behind. Edits code, but only to subtract; it never adds or retunes motion. Use when the user says the app "feels slow", "has too much animation", "feels over-animated", wants to "tone down the motion", or asks what animations to remove. For finding places that should animate, use find-animation-opportunities; for fixing animations that should stay, use improve-animations or review-animations.
skills.summary: Remove motion that makes an interface slower or harder to use.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: restraint
skills.title: Restraint
skills.description: Ships the smallest thing that does the job and deletes what nobody asked for.
skills.summary: Keep changes small, purposeful, and easy to review.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: reuse
skills.title: Reuse
skills.description: Reaches for the project's own components, then a maintained library, then a native feature, before writing new code.
skills.summary: Build with the project’s existing components and conventions.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: review-animations
skills.title: Review animations
skills.description: Reviews animation and motion code against a high craft bar derived from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy. Default to flagging; approval is earned.
skills.summary: Give motion code a focused, demanding second look.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: rule
skills.title: Rule
skills.description: Turns a repeated correction into a short project rule with the broken and fixed line, then applies it to existing code.
skills.summary: Turn a recurring correction into a clear project rule.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: scope
skills.title: Scope
skills.description: Changes exactly what was asked, keeps what already worked and finishes every item in the message.
skills.summary: Finish the requested work while preserving what already works.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: ship
skills.title: Ship
skills.description: Commits, pushes, merges and releases a change, watches the checks and confirms it is live.
skills.summary: Release a change, watch the checks, and confirm it is live.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: sketchbook
skills.title: Sketchbook
skills.description: Generates a daily batch of interaction experiments in the project's own stack as live tiles you keep or kill, learning your taste with every batch.
skills.summary: Explore small interaction ideas in a reusable visual workspace.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: stageshow
skills.title: Stageshow
skills.description: Build faux product UI that looks like a real product, as a still illustration or an animated demo with a cursor. Browser and app windows, dashboards, phones, notifications, terminals, bento grids and cursor walkthroughs, framed, masked and cropped the way a marketing page, feature card or docs hero needs them. Use whenever someone wants a fake or mocked UI, a product demo or walkthrough animation, a hero or feature-card illustration of an app, a product shot in the style of a polished marketing site, or an animated cursor doing things in an interface, even if they never say "faux UI". React and plain CSS.
skills.summary: Create believable product illustrations and animated walkthroughs.
skills.author: Benji Taylor

skills.name: verify
skills.title: Verify
skills.description: Checks a change in the running app before calling it done, then says where to see it.
skills.summary: Check the running result before calling the work done.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: viewports
skills.title: Viewports
skills.description: Renders a page at every width, each breakpoint edge, a short landscape phone and 200% text, then reports what overflows, clips or hides.
skills.summary: Check responsive layouts, breakpoint edges, and enlarged text.
skills.author: Raphael Salaja

skills.name: web-design-guidelines
skills.title: Web interface guidelines
skills.description: Review UI code for Web Interface Guidelines compliance. Use when asked to "review my UI", "check accessibility", "audit design", "review UX", or "check my site against best practices".
skills.summary: Review accessibility, forms, focus, motion, and interface behavior.
skills.author: Vercel

skills.name: write-swift
skills.title: Write Swift
skills.description: How to write modern Swift well — modeling with value types, Swift 6 data-race safety and approachable concurrency (@concurrent, main-actor-by-default, actors, task groups), protocols and generics (some vs any), API design, performance and ARC, Swift Testing, macros, and the modern language features agents don't know about yet. Use when writing, reviewing, or migrating Swift, or when a concurrency error, a hang, a data race, a retain cycle, or a performance problem needs fixing.
skills.summary: Write modern Swift with clear models and safe concurrency.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski
